Otoh why do you think that bills are going up.  Are you saying in quantity or in %? 

Quantity of total net issuance without regard to maturity is a function of

3) Change in SOMA (currently static)

If in % that is a policy decision regarding how much coupon debt vs bills is chosen to be issued AND the feds reinvestment policy which could change.  
One upward pressure on bills AND some of the coupons is the buyback program which so far is a WAM decreasing pressure 

Bills dollar issuance is going up for sure due to deficit.  BIlls % is a different question 

Thoughts?

I use Claude. GPT. Grok. Gemini. Hermes. Grokbot. Even Dot now.

they’re all useful for different things.

however, the annoying thing I find is that I get really comfortable with a model, then something new drops in the OpenAI eco that I want to try, but the last 3 months I’ve mostly been using Claude? 

FUCK. I’m back to square one.

well the way to fix this is with a harness.

What’s a harness? a harness is everything you build around your model which makes them become replaceable.

You do this by giving it context, memory, instructions, skills, tools, workflows so whenever you go from Claude to GPT, or GPT to Gemini, or Gemini to Grok you’re giving everything your brain (model) needs.

here’s how I’d make one:

1. download Obsidian

Create a vault called MY-AI.
This is the folder every AI will eventually work from.

2. create PROFILE. md

Tell it who you are, your goals, interests, preferences + how you like to work.
Only include information that actually helps an AI work with you.

3. create AGENTS. md

This is your rulebook.
Add how you want AI to research, reason, write + behave.
Tell it to read PROFILE. md, CURRENT. md + check /Skills before starting a task.

4. create CURRENT .md

Keep your current projects, priorities + open questions here.
Keep it short and update it often.

5. create /Skills

Every prompt/process you repeatedly use becomes a skill:
crypto-research. md
challenge-thesis. md
Write the steps once. Improve them over time. Reuse them everywhere.

6. create /Memory

Save important:
> research
> decisions
> lessons
> outcomes
Your agents can now learn from what you’ve already done instead of starting from zero.

7: create /Projects

Give every important project its own folder + a short README.md explaining the goal, status + next steps.

8: connect it

Open the MY-AI folder in Codex, Claude Code, Cursor etc.
They now work from the same context, rules, skills + memory.

9: back it up

Put MY-AI in a private Git repo.
Now your entire harness is portable + version controlled.

OKAY OKAY OKAY.

NFP - we had the best forecast for the third time in a row

Payrolls rose 29,000 against a consensus of 84-90,000, the unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2%, and average hourly earnings came in at 0.1% on the month against 0.3% expected, 3.0% on the year. Our withheld-taxes model had a base case just south of 40k, so we were almost spot on again. That is the third correct NFP call in a row, and on the Bloomberg ranking it makes us the best of all forecasters over that stretch (pretty proud about that coming from a little shop in Copenhagen/London). I mention it not to gloat (fine, a little) but because the model is doing exactly what it is built for: reading the tax receipts before the survey catches up.

The detail backs the soft read. Private payrolls rose 46,000 but government fell 17,000, education seasonals swung again, and the gains were concentrated in health care, construction and manufacturing while information, finance and energy shed jobs. Wage growth at 3.0% is not a number a central bank hikes on. The one soft spot in the soft read is that the unemployment rate rose partly because participation rose, which is a healthier reason than layoffs. The market took it the right way: October hike odds fell further, the front end rallied, the dollar gave back ground. Williams said one more and no rush. The data says maybe not even one.

Find out more at https://t.co/00SY5qimgl
